headline: U.S. Crude Stocks Rise as Product Ledgers Build
deck: Gasoline and distillate inventories rose, while crude stocks at the Cushing, Oklahoma, delivery hub declined.
body: U.S. commercial crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended 13 November, according to EIA data. The level was 3% below the five-year average, and the increase compared with a 58,000-barrel rise expected in a Reuters poll. [E1][E2][E3]
Crude stocks at the Cushing, Oklahoma, delivery hub fell by 1.2 million barrels. [E4]

Gasoline inventories increased by 5.2 million barrels and stood 3% above the five-year average. [E5] Distillate inventories, including diesel and heating oil, rose by 1.6 million barrels to 104.9 million barrels, compared with an expected 1.3 million-barrel increase. [E6]
Total commercial petroleum inventories increased by 9.2 million barrels for the week. [E7]
